name: Doodle Explainer
description: A1 and A2 combined: cream paper beats and near-black beats in one film, one coral accent, a drawn host (character x or y) in the corner, cards in the upper two thirds, and hand-drawn doodles (circles, underlines, arrows, checks, spark lines, icons) that draw themselves on the spoken word to explain the story.
rules: Alternate paper and dark beats (shot bg 'dark') inside one film; one coral accent for the key word of each beat.

The host is character x or y (presenter.look.character per shot, or tokens.presenter.character for the pack); the pose follows what is said: explaining for a concept, pointing at a card, thinking for a question, approval at the payoff.
Every beat gets at least one doodle that draws on a spoken word: scribble (circle, underline, box) around what matters, doodle (arrow, check, sparks, icon) for what it means.
One card in the upper 60 percent; doodles sit on it, never on the host.
native_moves: an arrow drawing from the host toward the card it explains
a circle drawn around the number the voice says

structures: claim, three doodled proofs, comment prompt
before and after of one workflow with a drawn arrow between
a list that is checked off line by line with drawn checks
openings: the host points at the claim card
a doodled question mark over the title
endings: comment-keyword card with a drawn arrow

camera_language: Locked frame; the motion is the host's pose swaps, the cards changing state and the doodles drawing on.
typography: word-pop captions; mono eyebrow above cards; serif italic for the accent word.
audio_direction: Steady low bed at -22 dB, a soft pen scratch under each doodle, a tick on each card change.
pitfalls: Do not draw doodles over the host's face.
Do not use more than three doodles on screen at once.
Do not mix coral with a second accent colour.
